body.x: In a data center, an energy storage system (ESS) facility or an electrical room, a fire detector or a camera can flag a problem long before a full emergency response begins. In the gap between the alarm and the arrival of firefighters, someone still has to find out where the fire is and how serious it looks, and walking toward a possible fire puts that person at risk.

3DT Solution, a technology company in Suseong-gu, Daegu, is developing a robot for that gap. Led by CEO Sangsu Kim, the company will exhibit its mobile safety robot ZEROS at FIX 2026, where ZEROS was recognized in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards. The company says it plans to introduce the ZEROS prototype and its key technologies to industry professionals, and to use the recognition and the exhibition to widen opportunities for field demonstrations, technology partnerships and commercialization.

According to 3DT Solution, ZEROS is a mobile safety robot that performs routine patrols and facility monitoring, investigates abnormal conditions, and supports an initial response when potential fire risks are detected. The company says it is not intended to replace existing fire detection systems or professional emergency response, but to complement the stage between detection and full-scale response. Kim is described in the application as a technology entrepreneur who draws on product design and prototyping experience to connect AI and robotics to safety problems at industrial sites.

The company says the robot combines a thermal imaging camera, an RGB-D camera, LiDAR and an inertial measurement unit (IMU), and is designed to merge AI-based visual analysis with thermal information to recognize its surroundings and identify potential signs of fire. It uses a mecanum-wheel omnidirectional mobile platform that moves forward, backward, sideways and in rotation, which 3DT Solution says is meant to give precise positioning where equipment and passageways limit mobility. ZEROS also has a sensor head controlled in yaw and pitch for directional observation and target tracking, a height-adjustable lifting mechanism for fire sources at different heights, and an integrated fire-suppression module. The company says it is developing the robot to approach a suspected fire location, search for the fire source, track and align with it, assess the situation at close range and support an initial response near the source. Its prototype work covers AI-based visual recognition, thermal imaging, RGB-D sensing, LiDAR and IMU-based perception, approach to a suspected fire location, target search, tracking and alignment, and integration of the lifting mechanism with the fire-suppression module.

3DT Solution sets ZEROS apart, in its words, by linking detection, movement, on-site verification, fire source tracking and alignment, and close-range initial response in one mobile platform, where fixed detectors only sense conditions from a set position. It adds that its in-house ability to integrate mechanical design, 3D modeling, prototyping, sensors and electronics, control systems and AI-based perception into working hardware lets it keep refining the robot. The company says it plans to develop autonomous navigation and mission-transition capabilities so that ZEROS can patrol, move to a location when an abnormal condition is detected, verify the situation and shift into an initial fire-response mission when needed. Its target customers are the operations and safety management teams at data centers, ESS facilities, electrical rooms and power facilities, precision manufacturing facilities and logistics centers, especially sites that run around the clock, spaces that are hard to monitor with people and environments that may be dangerous for workers to enter. The company names safety, facility and equipment managers and industrial safety officers as the likely purchasers, and says it also wants to work with industrial safety, fire protection equipment and robot system integration companies to link ZEROS with existing safety equipment.

On its background, 3DT Solution says it has built its capabilities through product design, prototyping and development projects with universities and industry in 3D modeling, mechanical design and 3D printing, including projects linked to Keimyung University, Kyungpook National University and Daegu Haany University. In 2026 it is developing and commercializing ZEROS through Korea's Youth Startup Academy deep-tech program while pursuing intellectual property protection for its core technologies.

At FIX 2026, the company wants to find partners for field demonstrations and technology collaboration, gather feedback on operating requirements in real industrial settings and feed it into development. It aims to build domestic field references and operational data, improve the robot's reliability and completeness, and move gradually to overseas opportunities through international exhibitions and partnerships.

3DT Solution has no overseas export sales and is concentrating on development, field demonstrations and commercialization in Korea. After completing domestic demonstrations, it plans to pursue markets such as the U.S., Japan and Singapore, where data centers, ESS facilities, advanced manufacturing and logistics infrastructure are widely operated. It will consider both direct exports and collaboration with local robotics, industrial safety, fire protection and system integration partners. The company expects hurdles in different safety, fire protection and certification requirements by country, in validating reliability in real industrial environments and in building local maintenance and technical support networks, since ZEROS combines mobile robotics, AI recognition, thermal imaging and a fire-suppression module. Its plan is to accumulate operating data and field references in Korea first, then review the regulations and certification requirements in each target market and set up local partners for installation, operation, maintenance and after-sales support.

In the short term, it will keep developing ZEROS's core functions and hardware and run field demonstrations in Korea, aiming to integrate AI-based visual recognition and thermal information, autonomous navigation and localization, fire source search, tracking and alignment, and lifting and fire-suppression systems into a platform suited to industrial sites. Next, it will expand demonstrations in data centers, ESS facilities, electrical rooms, manufacturing facilities and logistics centers to collect operating data and validate practical requirements such as installation, operation, maintenance and integration with existing safety infrastructure. Over the medium to long term, it plans to develop ZEROS from an initial fire-response device into an autonomous industrial safety robotics platform.

FIX 2026 is the third edition of a future-industry exhibition that brings together and connects innovative technologies in future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. It will run from Wednesday, Oct. 21, to Saturday, Oct. 24, at EXCO in Daegu. Under the theme "AI, Beyond Tech into Reality," it offers AI-based technology exhibitions, conferences and lectures by experts from Korea and abroad, and networking programs that share industry trends and core technologies.
